GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is South Labuhanbatu Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.

4. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion either directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
5. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
6. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a Child who is still in the womb.
7. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
8. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against Children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of Children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences violence and/or threat of violence.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from acts of Violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
15. Gender is the difference in characteristics, roles, functions and status between Women and men which is not based on biological differences, but rather based on socio-cultural relations influenced by the broader structure of society.
16. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate Gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region.

18. 19. Safe House is a shelter/temporary protection house for Victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of Victims from threats and danger from perpetrators, and is only known by relevant parties such as certain personnel at UPT P2TP2A for reasons of Victim safety and security.
20. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard steps that must be taken in protecting Victims starting from complaints/identification, rehabilitation, health, Social Rehabilitation, advocacy up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or Victims.
21. Family is the smallest unit in Society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child or Family by blood in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree and/or if any up to the fourth degree.
22. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have Family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, representation, and/or Household workers and reside in that Household.
23. Community is individuals, Families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
24. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of South Labuhanbatu Regency.
25. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out their social functions properly in Community life.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Based on empirical evidence, it is revealed that Women and Children are groups that frequently become victims of violence. Many factors cause the occurrence of violence against Women and Children, among them is the patriarchal cultural factor that still widely occurs in society which views Women as lower than men. In addition, incorrect perceptions about violence against Women and Children are also still commonly found, which consider violence as a normal matter and a right of the perpetrator. Violence against Women and Children can be viewed from the type, perpetrator, location of incident, time, age and consequences of the act of violence. Violence against Women and Children as mentioned above applies generally and has no relevance to the type of education, occupation and income, social position, religion and belief, nationality, ethnicity and race attached to men and Women. This means that in all types of social strata, violence against Women and Children can and continues to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and Women is still believed and manifested in social life. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in South Labuhanbatu Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, a legal umbrella in the form of regional regulations is required.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.
The formulation of this Regional Regulation on Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is intended to provide a legal foundation for the Regional Government in providing protection for Women and Children in the area of South Labuhanbatu Regency.

Article 10

d. acts that result in economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the Victim is under the control of that person.

Article 11

b. acts with or without the consent of the Victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or Services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the Victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Based on empirical evidence, it is revealed that Women and Children are groups that frequently become victims of violence. Many factors cause the occurrence of violence against Women and Children, among them is the patriarchal cultural factor that still widely occurs in society which views Women as lower than men. In addition, incorrect perceptions about violence against Women and Children are also still commonly found, which consider violence as a normal matter and a right of the perpetrator. Violence against Women and Children can be viewed from the type, perpetrator, location of incident, time, age and consequences of the act of violence. Violence against Women and Children as mentioned above applies generally and has no relevance to the type of education, occupation and income, social position, religion and belief, nationality, ethnicity and race attached to men and Women. This means that in all types of social strata, violence against Women and Children can and continues to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and Women is still believed and manifested in social life. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in South Labuhanbatu Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, a legal umbrella in the form of regional regulations is required.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.
The formulation of this Regional Regulation on Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is intended to provide a legal foundation for the Regional Government in providing protection for Women and Children in the area of South Labuhanbatu Regency.

I. GENERAL
Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Based on empirical evidence, it is revealed that Women and Children are groups that frequently become victims of violence. Many factors cause the occurrence of violence against Women and Children, among them is the patriarchal cultural factor that still widely occurs in society which views Women as lower than men. In addition, incorrect perceptions about violence against Women and Children are also still commonly found, which consider violence as a normal matter and a right of the perpetrator. Violence against Women and Children can be viewed from the type, perpetrator, location of incident, time, age and consequences of the act of violence. Violence against Women and Children as mentioned above applies generally and has no relevance to the type of education, occupation and income, social position, religion and belief, nationality, ethnicity and race attached to men and Women. This means that in all types of social strata, violence against Women and Children can and continues to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and Women is still believed and manifested in social life. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in South Labuhanbatu Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, a legal umbrella in the form of regional regulations is required.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.
The formulation of this Regional Regulation on Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is intended to provide a legal foundation for the Regional Government in providing protection for Women and Children in the area of South Labuhanbatu Regency.

I. GENERAL
Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Based on empirical evidence, it is revealed that Women and Children are groups that frequently become victims of violence. Many factors cause the occurrence of violence against Women and Children, among them is the patriarchal cultural factor that still widely occurs in society which views Women as lower than men. In addition, incorrect perceptions about violence against Women and Children are also still commonly found, which consider violence as a normal matter and a right of the perpetrator. Violence against Women and Children can be viewed from the type, perpetrator, location of incident, time, age and consequences of the act of violence. Violence against Women and Children as mentioned above applies generally and has no relevance to the type of education, occupation and income, social position, religion and belief, nationality, ethnicity and race attached to men and Women. This means that in all types of social strata, violence against Women and Children can and continues to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and Women is still believed and manifested in social life. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in South Labuhanbatu Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, a legal umbrella in the form of regional regulations is required.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.
The formulation of this Regional Regulation on Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is intended to provide a legal foundation for the Regional Government in providing protection for Women and Children in the area of South Labuhanbatu Regency.

7. Woman is a person who is female in gender.

Article 27
(1) Regional Government through regional apparatus with authority over Women and Children shall compile data and information regarding the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence.

d. acts that result in economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the Victim is under the control of that person.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of Human Rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination. Based on empirical evidence, it is revealed that Women and Children are groups that frequently become victims of violence. Many factors cause the occurrence of violence against Women and Children, among them is the patriarchal cultural factor that still widely occurs in society which views Women as lower than men. In addition, incorrect perceptions about violence against Women and Children are also still commonly found, which consider violence as a normal matter and a right of the perpetrator. Violence against Women and Children can be viewed from the type, perpetrator, location of incident, time, age and consequences of the act of violence. Violence against Women and Children as mentioned above applies generally and has no relevance to the type of education, occupation and income, social position, religion and belief, nationality, ethnicity and race attached to men and Women. This means that in all types of social strata, violence against Women and Children can and continues to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and Women is still believed and manifested in social life. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in South Labuhanbatu Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, a legal umbrella in the form of regional regulations is required.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations that can guarantee its implementation are needed.
The formulation of this Regional Regulation on Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is intended to provide a legal foundation for the Regional Government in providing protection for Women and Children in the area of South Labuhanbatu Regency.

7. Woman is a person who is female in gender.

13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will, is, or has occurred.

15. Gender is the difference in characteristics, roles, functions and status between Women and men which is not based on biological differences, but rather based on socio-cultural relations influenced by the broader structure of society.

19. Article 10
Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d is caused by: a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of a Child properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for care; b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a Child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians or any other party responsible for their care; c. acts that neglect a person within the scope of their Household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
d. acts that result in economic dependence by means of restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the Victim is under the control of that person.

Article 18
In order to provide Services and protection to Women and Children from acts of Violence, the Regional Government establishes P2TP2A.

Article 27
(1) Regional Government through regional apparatus with authority over Women and Children shall compile data and information regarding the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence.

c. Women and Children at risk or vulnerable; and

Article 14
The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility for the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
